title: Initial investigation & the USG approach
guide: Three arms — USG abdomen (the most important investigation), RFT (urea, creatinine, Na+, K+) and urine analysis (24 hr protein preferred, plus albumin and protein ratios). Look for size <8 cm, 8–10 cm with loss of CMD, and >10 cm with loss of CMD in DM/HIV/amyloidosis; the normal-kidney figure labels cortex isoechoic, pyramid hypoechoic and fat/calyx/sinus/vessels hyperechoic.

title: CKD mimics: hydronephroureteronephrosis & the AKI arm
guide: Rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis before diagnosing CKD (prominent calyces, visible ureter). The hours-to-days tempo is AKI: postrenal B/L hydroureteronephrosis (USG), pre-renal with normal urine analysis, and the page's 'acute tubular/interstitial nephrosis'.

title: Rapidly progressive failure, vascular causes & RAS words
guide: Days to weeks = RPRF (RPGN m/c, biopsy; severe ATN and TMA bracketed as rare causes); hypertensive crisis = vascular: RAS (large vessel) and TMA (small vessel); normal RFT with renal disease = nephrotic syndrome, RTA I/II, asymptomatic urine abnormality. RAS is also renovascular hypertension/renal artery occlusion disease and progresses to ischemic nephropathy.

title: RAS: who gets what, and the Goldblatt model
guide: Overall atherosclerosis (proximal 1–2 cm, symptomatic >80%); young population FMD/arteriopathy (mid to distal); Indian/Asian Takayasu (proximal, F:m 9:1); young males PAN (entire length, microaneurysm). Types are explained by the Goldblatt two kidney one clip model.

title: Unilateral RAS: pathogenesis of the small kidney
guide: Asymmetric kidney size (also seen in reflux). Affected side: ↓RBF →(+) RAS →(+) aldosterone → ↑↑AT-II → profound vasoconstriction → HTN/HTN crisis, with persistent hypertension and normal RFT/urine. Contralateral side: ↑RBF/medullary flow → ↑RIHP → ↓PCT reabsorption → natriuresis (pressure natriuresis theory). Potency order: urotensin > endothelin > AT-II.

title: Diagnosing RAS and treating unilateral disease
guide: USG clue is an asymmetric kidney; screening = renal doppler; confirm with CT renal angiography or MR angiography (IOC), the captioned figure being 'unilateral renal artery stenosis'. Treatment: ACE inhibitors/ARBs are DOC; PTRA only if the kidney is >8 cm.

title: Bilateral RAS: volume overload, flash edema & treatment
guide: Poor prognosis. Both arteries are crossed ('x – Occlusion'); ↓RBF raises renin but the natriuresis escape is lost (↓RIHP), so Na+/water retention → intravascular volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema (d/t intravascular edema) → B/L PTRA with stenting. For BP: diuretics are DOC, ACE inhibitors/ARBs are contraindicated (↓GFR); stop smoking, start statins.

title: Colour doppler cut-offs, angiography & fibromuscular dysplasia
guide: Every pulmonary edema is cardiac until proven otherwise. CDU looks for parvus tardus and RI: ≥0.8 = parenchymal disease/CKD; <0.8 with PSV >180 cm/s, RAR >3.5 or ΔRI >0.05 → CT/MR angiography (IOC), also for inconclusive studies; conventional angiography is the gold standard and is both diagnostic and therapeutic. FMD: young girls, non-atherosclerotic non-inflammatory arteriopathy, middle–distal artery, medial fibroplasia, 25% bilateral renal and 25% cerebral, string of beads, treated by PTRA with good prognosis.
